newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana killer executed by lethal injection.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana killer executed by lethal injection.

text.p: A Louisiana man convicted of fatally stabbing a restaurant patron 13 times during a 1984 robbery was executed by lethal injection early on Thursday morning.

John Ashley Brown Jr., 35, was pronounced dead at 12:12 a.m. local time (0612 GMT), officials at the Louisiana State Penitentiary announced. It was the first execution in the state in more than a year.
Brown was convicted in 1985 of murdering Omer Laughlin, 53, as he and his wife left a New Orleans restaurant and walked to their car.

Brown's execution was stayed three times after he was moved to Death Row in 1985. Twice on Wednesday the U.S. Supreme Court refused to block the execution, and Gov. Mike Foster also refused to intervene.

According to prison spokeswoman Cathy Jett, Brown's last words were, "I just want to make a short statement, to let my baby sister know I love you and to (tell) the rest of my family for supporting me, I love you. That's all."
For his last meal, the former drug user selected boiled crawfish, crackers, a lettuce, tomato and onion salad with ranch dressing, apple pie, Neopolitan ice cream and two chocolate malts.
